scenes.tts: Tap the tendon below your kneecap, and your leg kicks. What happens to the muscle on the other side of the joint?
scenes.visual: A leg in profile; a reflex hammer taps the tendon below the kneecap and the lower leg kicks. The hamstrings on the back of the thigh are outlined with a question mark.
scenes.narration: Tap the tendon below your kneecap, and your leg kicks. What happens to the muscle on the other side of the joint?

scenes.tts: The tap stretches the quadriceps. Inside it lie stretch sensors called muscle spindles.
scenes.visual: Zoom into the quadriceps: a muscle spindle, a slim capsule, among the muscle fibres. Label: muscle spindle.
scenes.narration: The tap stretches the quadriceps. Inside it lie stretch sensors called muscle spindles.

scenes.tts: A spindle lies alongside the force-making fibres. It lengthens with the muscle, so it reports stretch.
scenes.visual: The spindle lies parallel to the force-making fibres, like a thread laid along a rope. The muscle lengthens and the spindle stretches with it. Label: senses stretch.
scenes.narration: A spindle lies alongside the force-making fibres. It lengthens with the muscle, so it reports stretch.

scenes.tts: Its sensory axons, or afferents, carry signals into the cord. The main ones are called one A fibres.
scenes.caption: Its sensory axons, or afferents, carry signals into the cord. The main ones are called Ia fibres.
scenes.visual: An axon leaves the spindle toward the cord. Labels: afferent = sensory axon carrying signals into the cord; Ia fibre (said one-A), from an old numbering of fibres by thickness: among the thickest and fastest.
scenes.narration: Its sensory axons, or afferents, carry signals into the cord. The main ones are called Ia fibres.

scenes.tts: The tap makes them fire. They enter the cord through the dorsal root, and they branch.
scenes.visual: Spikes run along the Ia fibre into the dorsal root of a spinal cord cross-section, where the fibre splits into two branches.
scenes.narration: The tap makes them fire. They enter the cord through the dorsal root, and they branch.

scenes.tts: One branch excites the quadriceps motor neurons directly. That is one synapse. The pool goes up, and the leg kicks.
scenes.visual: One branch contacts a quadriceps motor neuron. Its voltage bar rises past threshold. A counter reads synapses: 1. The leg kicks.
scenes.narration: One branch excites the quadriceps motor neurons directly. That is one synapse. The pool goes up, and the leg kicks.

scenes.tts: But the motor neurons of the hamstrings, on the back of the thigh, are held back. A one A fibre only ever excites. How can it hold anything back?
scenes.caption: But the motor neurons of the hamstrings, on the back of the thigh, are held back. A Ia fibre only ever excites. How can it hold anything back?
scenes.visual: The hamstring motor neurons' voltage bars dip; an already active hamstring trace weakens. Question card: The Ia fibre only excites. How can it inhibit anything?
scenes.narration: But the motor neurons of the hamstrings, on the back of the thigh, are held back. A Ia fibre only ever excites. How can it hold anything back?

scenes.tts: Its second branch excites an inhibitory interneuron, on the same side of the cord.
scenes.visual: The second branch contacts a small interneuron, coloured red, on the same side. Label: Ia inhibitory interneuron.
scenes.narration: Its second branch excites an inhibitory interneuron, on the same side of the cord.

scenes.tts: That interneuron inhibits the hamstring motor neurons. Their pool goes down. This path has two synapses.
scenes.visual: The interneuron contacts a hamstring motor neuron; its voltage bar is pushed down, away from threshold. The counter reads synapses: 2.
scenes.narration: That interneuron inhibits the hamstring motor neurons. Their pool goes down. This path has two synapses.

scenes.tts: In this pathway, the excitatory Ia fibre inhibits the antagonist through an inhibitory interneuron.
scenes.visual: Card: Ia afferent excites inhibitory interneuron, which inhibits antagonist motor neurons.
scenes.narration: In this pathway, the excitatory Ia fibre inhibits the antagonist through an inhibitory interneuron.

scenes.tts: One stretch, two commands, to two pools. Sherrington called this pairing reciprocal innervation.
scenes.visual: Both paths shown at once: quadriceps pool up (green), hamstring pool down (red). Label: reciprocal innervation (Sherrington).
scenes.narration: One stretch, two commands, to two pools. Sherrington called this pairing reciprocal innervation.

scenes.tts: A second sensor shows why the spindle needs help. The Golgi tendon organ sits where muscle meets tendon.
scenes.visual: Split screen: the spindle lying alongside the fibres, and several Golgi tendon organs at the muscle-tendon junction, each in line with a small group of fibres, like links in a chain.
scenes.narration: A second sensor shows why the spindle needs help. The Golgi tendon organ sits where muscle meets tendon.

scenes.tts: Each one lies in line with a few fibres and senses their pull. Together they signal force, not length.
scenes.visual: Arrows of pull from a few fibres pass through each tendon organ. Labels: spindle = length; tendon organs = force.
scenes.narration: Each one lies in line with a few fibres and senses their pull. Together they signal force, not length.

scenes.tts: A unit pulling on one tendon organ twitches, so that organ fires. The shortened spindle can fall slack and go quiet.
scenes.visual: A unit whose fibres attach to one tendon organ twitches, and the muscle shortens a little. That organ's trace fires a burst; the spindle sags and its trace goes quiet.
scenes.narration: A unit pulling on one tendon organ twitches, so that organ fires. The shortened spindle can fall slack and go quiet.

scenes.tts: That slack spindle is a problem. Gamma motor neurons fix it.
scenes.visual: Replay: the muscle shortens, the spindle goes slack, its trace goes flat.
scenes.narration: That slack spindle is a problem. Gamma motor neurons fix it.

scenes.tts: They supply only the spindle, and they contract its two ends.
scenes.visual: A thin gamma motor axon runs to the spindle's two poles, which contract. Label: gamma motor neuron.
scenes.narration: They supply only the spindle, and they contract its two ends.

scenes.tts: That pulls the centre of the spindle taut again, where the one A endings wrap.
scenes.caption: That pulls the centre of the spindle taut again, where the Ia endings wrap.
scenes.visual: The spindle's centre, wrapped by the Ia ending, pulls taut; its trace resumes firing.
scenes.narration: That pulls the centre of the spindle taut again, where the Ia endings wrap.

scenes.tts: Think of a tape measure that winds itself in, so it never goes loose.
scenes.visual: A tape measure winding itself in as two points move closer, staying taut.
scenes.narration: Think of a tape measure that winds itself in, so it never goes loose.

scenes.tts: When alpha and gamma motor neurons fire together, the spindle can stay in range during a contraction.
scenes.visual: Alpha and gamma motor neurons fire together; the muscle shortens while the spindle stays taut and keeps firing. Label: alpha-gamma coactivation.
scenes.narration: When alpha and gamma motor neurons fire together, the spindle can stay in range during a contraction.

scenes.tts: So ask the two questions of any reflex. A stretch pushes its own muscle's pool up and its antagonist's pool down.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: Which pools go up, which down? Stretch: own muscle up (1 synapse), antagonist down (2 synapses). Gamma drive keeps the spindle signalling.
scenes.narration: So ask the two questions of any reflex. A stretch pushes its own muscle's pool up and its antagonist's pool down.

scenes.tts: And gamma drive keeps the spindle signalling while the muscle shortens.
scenes.visual: The takeaway card's last line lights: gamma drive keeps the spindle signalling.
scenes.narration: And gamma drive keeps the spindle signalling while the muscle shortens.
